html:
Company rule in India was the period when the East India Company, a London trading company, governed much of India with its own army. On the 1815 map its lands stretch from Bengal and the Ganges plain down the east coast to the far south.

The Company's rule began with victory at the Battle of Plassey in 1757. By the Treaty of Allahabad in 1765 it won the right to collect the revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha. Governor General Richard Wellesley spread its power with subsidiary alliances, defeated Mysore in 1799 and took Delhi in 1803.

In 1813 Parliament ended the Company's monopoly on trade with India, so it became more a government than a business. It won the Third Anglo-Maratha War of 1817 to 1818 and then most of the subcontinent. After the Indian Rebellion of 1857 the British Crown took over, and the British Raj began in 1858.
